extraction.name: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series)
extraction.description: PASTIS is the first large-scale, publicly available Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations. It comprises 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128, with each sequence containing between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019, for a total of over 2 billion pixels. The dataset spans over 4000 km² across four different regions of France with diverse climates and crop distributions. Each pixel is associated with a semantic label from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class, and each non-background pixel has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. In total, 124,422 parcels are individualized, each with their bounding box, pixel-precise mask, and crop type.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu
extraction.publisher: LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The SITS of PASTIS are taken from 4 different Sentinel-2 tiles in different regions of the French metropolitan territory. These regions cover a wide variety of climates and culture distributions. Sentinel tiles span 100×100km and have a spatial resolution of 10 meter per pixel. Each of these tiles is subdivided in square patches of size 1.28×1.28km (128×128 pixels at 10m/pixel), for a total of around 24,000 patches. 2,433 patches (~10% of all available patches) were selected, favoring patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: We estimate that close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. Even after the automatic filtering of predominantly cloudy acquisitions, some patches are still partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The satellite images used in PASTIS were gathered from THEIA using Copernicus data from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform. The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite, after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel. All bands except the atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10 were selected.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The temporal sampling of the sequences in PASTIS is irregular: depending on their location, patches are observed a different number of times and at different intervals. This is a result of both the orbit schedule of Sentinel-2 and the policy of Sentinel data providers not to process tile observations identified as covered by clouds for more than 90% of the tile's surface. The time between acquisitions is uneven with a median of 5 days. This lack of regularity is due to the automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover by the satellite data provider THEIA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each Sentinel-2 tile is subdivided in square patches of size 1.28×1.28km (128×128 pixels at 10m/pixel). The parcels' extents are cropped along the extent of their 128×128 patch, and the bounding boxes are modified accordingly. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are annotated with the void label. All-zeroes images are appended at the end of shorter sequences to match the length of the longer sequence in the batch to facilitate handling of batches by the GPU. A padding mask is retained to prevent the spatial and temporal encoding of padded values, and to exclude these padded values from temporal averages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS). The FLPIS allows retrieval of the extent and content of all parcels within the tiles, as reported by the farmers. Each patch pixel is annotated with a semantic label corresponding to either the parcels' crop type or the background class. The pixels of each unique parcel in the patch receive a corresponding instance label. The FLPIS uses a 73 class breakdown for crop types. Classes with at least 400 parcels and with samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles were selected, leading to an 18-classes nomenclature. Parcels belonging to classes not in the 18-classes nomenclature are annotated with the void label. Pixels which are not within the extent of any declared parcel are annotated with the background 'stuff' label. The FLPIS allows retrieval of the pixel-precise borders of each parcel, and bounding boxes are computed for each parcel.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are annotated with the void label. Predicted parcels which overlap with an IoU superior to 0.5 with a void parcel are not counted as false positive or true positive, but are simply ignored by the metric. The void class is reserved for out-of-scope parcels, either because their crop type is not in the nomenclature or because their overlap with the selected square patch is too small.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is split into 5 folds, chosen with a 1km buffer between images to avoid cross-fold contamination. The official 5-fold cross-validation scheme is provided. Geo-referencing metadata of the patches and parcels is included in PASTIS, allowing for the constitution of geographically consistent folds to evaluate spatial generalization.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for a fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (~50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and in the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. More generally, the automated analysis of SITS represents a significant interest for a wide range of applications, such as surveying urban development and deforestation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. Patches were selected favoring patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance of the dataset. The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The temporal sampling of the sequences is irregular, with sequences comprising 33 to 61 acquisitions depending on location. Close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. The dataset covers only four different regions of France, which may limit generalization to other geographic areas or climates. The dataset is restricted to agricultural parcels and does not provide extensive land-cover prediction beyond the background class.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is designed for panoptic segmentation of agricultural parcels from time series of satellite images, including both semantic segmentation (crop type classification) and instance segmentation (individual parcel delineation). It can be used for crop mapping, monitoring agricultural subsidies allocation, ensuring crop rotation practices, and other Earth observation tasks involving temporal dynamics.
